title: S. Korea Cracks Down on Overcharging of Tourists
paragraphs: In some places, it's common for tourists to pay higher prices. In India, for example, visitors often pay at least 10 times more than locals to see historical monuments.
Known as "tiered pricing" or "dual pricing," the idea is that the extra money helps pay for maintenance of popular sites, while keeping prices low enough that locals can still enjoy them.
That's official dual pricing — and the separate prices will be listed publicly for everyone to see.
But as places become popular with tourists, local shops may also start charging visitors more without telling them.
This has been happening in South Korea — and to stop it, the government has introduced stronger rules and penalties for hotels, restaurants and taxis that overcharge tourists.

Previously, some of these businesses would just receive a warning. But the government introduced new rules for general accommodations in mid-July, and has now added similar ones for homes offering accommodation to tourists.
Under the new rules, any accommodations that overcharge tourists or don't show their prices clearly will be suspended for five days.

Accommodations caught breaking the rules a second time will have their business suspended for 10 days, up from seven days previously. Those breaking the rules a third time will be suspended for 20 days, up from 15.
Guesthouses and accommodations like Airbnbs — which previously did not have to clearly show their prices — will also have to follow these rules.
Restaurant owners will face similar penalties, according to The Korea Times.
Meanwhile, taxi drivers found overcharging tourists will lose their license for 30 days. A second offense will lead to a 60-day suspension, while a third offense could mean losing their license.
The government also plans to introduce penalties for business owners who cancel reservations without valid reasons.
Officials hope the changes will help tourists in South Korea have a more enjoyable stay — and encourage new tourists to visit!
